name: psldram
transitions: real->protected (CR0.PE 0->1, CS far-jump to 32-bit flat code segment 0x08)
build PD+PT0(identity code window)+PT1(fresh non-identity data page linear 0x400000 -> phys 0x900000)
CR3 load + CR0.PG 0->1 (paging ON, 4 KiB pages)
B) 16-bit store->same-addr RMW load: mov w[0x400010],0xC57C; sub w[0x400010],0x3A84; ebx=0x8AF8
C) byte store->same-addr RMW load: mov b[0x400020],0xAA; add b[0x400020],0x11; ecx=0xBB
D) POP word [m]->SUB word [m] (CWSDPMI shape): pop w[0x400030]=0x3B48; sub w[0x400030],0x3A84; edx=0x00C4
clean exit via isa-debug-exit (out 0xf4,al al=0x42 -> qemu status 133)
description: Paged store->load RAW (read-after-write) regression guard (task #102 DOS-Quake). A back-to-back store -> same-address RMW-load (32/16/8-bit + the exact CWSDPMI POP-word-[m]/SUB-word-[m] shape) into a FRESHLY-mapped non-identity paged page that was never read before, so a write-allocate stale-line or store->load forwarding bug would surface as a read-back GPR divergence. The earlier 'SUB reads stale 0' store->load-hazard hypothesis was DISPROVEN by a cycle-level BFM mem-port trace (the RMW load reads exactly the prior store's value); this test pins that correct behaviour. Per-record differential vs qemu-system-i386 (no interrupts -> the gdbstub single-step golden delivers the whole run).
